# Independent Julia GPU PhysCal fixture (#636)

`physcal_julia_l128.txt` was generated by `gen_physcal_julia.jl` from unmodified
Julia-mVMC `611031147f1bad9704c55084f6817feeba481b13`, Juliaup `+1.13` resolving
to Julia 1.13.3. The byte-identical `test/gpu/Manifest-v1.13.toml` has SHA-256
`86c69ea3a0c04c2b6af6f48a3f36ec2a08fa2bc564ac4845f5799e53244fc573`.

Linux x86_64, RTX 3060 (physical GPU 0), driver 580.178.04, CUDA.jl 6.4.2,
CUDA runtime 13.4.0, cuRAND 10.4.4, cuBLAS 13.8.0, cuSOLVER 12.3.4.
Rust uses NVRTC 12.8, cuRAND 10.3.9, cuBLAS 12.8.4 and cuSOLVER 11.7.3.
The software stacks are recorded separately.

The common L128 fixed parameter file has SHA-256
`9130219b4af78438bee2f30171833e7a8f86a01ff11e23276af439652230fd90`.
The fixture uses two XORWOW-initialized walkers, seed 79, and a deterministic
20-hop supplied UInt32 tape. Three product-side Green operators supplement
the input's 256 one-body and 768 direct two-body terms. Products are evaluated
per walker before averaging; multiplying ensemble means would fail this case.

Configuration integers, acceptance counts and supplied words are exact.
Initial parameters use `1e-14 + 1e-14 max(abs(a),abs(b))`; Pfaffians use
`1e-12 + 5e-11 max(abs(a),abs(b))`; fixed-state observable means use
`1e-10 + 1e-10 max(abs(a),abs(b))`. The first numerical difference is in the
independent factor/inverse calculation, with maximum Pfaffian relative error
`5.446e-13`. Maximum observable absolute differences are `2.843e-14` before
sampling and `3.411e-13` after the supplied tape. These are the existing GPU
Opt stage bounds for conditioned 128-electron QP matrices and dot reductions;
they do not excuse RNG or configuration differences. A separate exact next-word
check proves that supplying the tape does not consume the resident XORWOW RNG.
The 20-window test checks repeatability across an intervening differently seeded
run and requires no explicit host/device transfers during sampling/measurement.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  julia +1.13 --startup-file=no --project=/path/to/Julia-mVMC/test/gpu \
  gpu/mvmc-gpu-cuda/tests/fixtures/gen_physcal_julia.jl \
  benchmark/cpu_scaling_l128/inputs/phys/namelist.def \
  benchmark/cpu_scaling_l128/inputs/phys/zqp_opt.dat \
  gpu/mvmc-gpu-cuda/tests/fixtures/physcal_julia_l128.txt
```

Fixture SHA-256:
`392074512757690a4dc6e2c2bf6afa445993602fe45168fa0d76d2ddb799e541`.
Normal Rust tests only read this committed fixture and never invoke Julia.
